pitch_detail.notes: An easy, bushy groove that gets you onto the east end of the ledge system. You only need it if you came up Dragon's Tail Couloir; hiking west around the ledges skips it. Easy but unpleasant, so most parties avoid it.

Two ways to reach the base of pitch 3. One is a blocky dihedral about 30 feet left of the Dragon Slayer crack, probably 5.6/5.7. If that is wet, use the line roughly 80 feet left: easy protectable slab to a grassy ledge, a chimney with a few 5.5 moves, then a gully or an unprotected slab to a ramp that ends at the southeast edge of the prow. One 70 m rope covers it.

The first real difficulty: an unprotectable 5.6 start on lichen-covered, loose rock just right of the arete, then a 40 foot wall to a big ledge. Traverse that ledge right onto the east face for roughly 300 feet, through thorny bushes, stopping where rope drag gets bad. A short extra pitch may be needed to finish the traverse. Once across, retreat is hard.

Aim for the tree above. Protect the short wall (one 5.6 move) with a #3 or #4, then pull through an awkward dirty funnel past the tree and around the corner. Run the rope up and left on easy ground to a large ledge below a notch between two spires. A 70 m rope almost reaches the ledge.

Easy to lose the line. Skip the harder dihedrals and flaky cracks straight up; take a rocky ramp toward another tree and a big moss patch on the skyline, continuing around the spire. Protect one short dirty move and keep spiraling until the last pitches to the summit are visible.

Hardest pitch. About 5.7 moves with poor protection lead into a deep water groove; solid gear comes about 50 feet up. Then follow a straight dihedral, with a small overhang that takes a #3, weaving between it and the groove to a big ledge under the summit. A limber pine there makes a belay. Dirty rock; placing gear takes thought.
Short and easy: protectable ledges from the limber pine to the summit block. The summit is large and comfortable.

review.changed: Wrote all seven pitches with stated grades and lengths. No rappel table: one rappel station is mentioned (35 m east into Dragon's Tail Couloir), not a station-by-station list.
review.other_findings: Stated pitch lengths add to about 375 m versus stored length_m 305 (pitch 3 includes a ~300 ft traverse). Stored pitches 7 and descent text agree.

pitch_detail.notes: Easy broken ground up and left leads to a slightly overhanging hand crack in a big boulder; pull the overhang on good jams and follow the crack to a large ledge below the main crack (optional belay). Then fire up the steep crack with hand and thin-hand jams, past some pods and a very short leftward traverse at the crux, finishing in a thin finger crack that reaches the arete. Cams from 0.3 to 3, doubles of 0.75-2, a few nuts.

Follow the clear line on the arete and break right past a gap onto a huge ledge. Belay there or a little higher among the boulders. Short and easy. Descent: rappel from slings with a rap ring just below the ledge to the west, or scramble up and walk down Big Blue.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. A 3-pitch split is possible for rope drag; kept the 2 described. No lengths, bolts or pitch-2 grade stated. Only one rappel anchor mentioned, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Mixed terrain up the gully, climbing over chockstones, which form the crux. Belay on the big ledge of broken rock above.

Protect the belay, then climb snice and ice, with a handful of mixed moves. Belay in rock outcrops on the left, from where you can scramble off west. Bring stubby screws, nuts, cams to #2, knifeblades and Lost Arrows.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. Forms briefly in a melt-freeze cycle on a cold overcast day; watch avalanche conditions. Descent: traverse west and pick a gully.
review.other_findings: Stored grade WI3- M3; both pitches are given as WI3 M3.

pitch_detail.notes: Huge boulders block the creek. Hike around to the north, or squeeze up the slot on the right wall if its ice is good. Mixed difficulty is easy.
Climb the slot. If it has no ice, the rest of the route is probably out of shape.
A pillar or curtain to a ramp, then over the top of the bulge. Belay from the boulder in the creek or a chockstone 20 feet back. A good sample of the route.
An ice ramp just up canyon that may be buried; approach with caution in very deep snow. Then slog on to the main ice.
Another pillar leads to a massive trough, where easy ice goes left, right or straight up. Belay with screws on the roomy ledge behind the main pillar.
Climb the exposed pillar for 70 or 80 feet, then keep going through the narrow slot onto a platform. The belay is the arch on the left.
A short chunk of ice just past the pillar, then about 500 feet up the creek to a small amphitheater; the slog is surprisingly cruxy.
One detached pillar, topping out at a tree on the upper left.

rappel_detail.notes: Single rope. Below it, either downclimb the little step or use willows or trees on the descender's left.
Use two ropes; one rope might reach but is untested.

rappel_detail.anchor: main pillar, or a V-thread if the ice is trustworthy
rappel_detail.notes: Simul-rappel with two ropes. Then downclimb the low-angle creek ice or rappel from trees or boulders.
Single rope. Downclimb pitch 2 (best) or rig something off boulders or rim trees to the north; bypass pitch 1.

review.changed: Wrote all eight labelled pitches (including the 3.5 and 5.5 segments) with converted lengths, and a four-station descent table. Lengths were stated in feet.
review.other_findings: Stored 6 pitches; six numbered plus two half-pitches are described. Two 70 m ropes and a v-threader recommended.

pitch_detail.notes: Angle up and right across grassy ledges to the foot of a right-facing corner system. At least 200 feet; the exact length is uncertain.
Traverse right across the face into a long left-facing corner and follow it to ledges, about 200 feet. A pin may sit at one of the belays along here.

Cut left across the face toward the prow with the large roof and belay near a left-facing dihedral, about 300 feet. Overshooting leads next to the KT chimney, from where you must come back right to find the corner.
Follow the corner up until the ramp ends, about 100 feet.
Easy ground trending left to reach the upper KT chimney, about 100 feet.
The deep chimney, with fun stemming, then left through a big tunnel to a platform under the headwall, about 200 feet.
The short headwall via a finger crack to the summit, about 100 feet.

review.changed: Wrote all seven pitches; lengths in feet were rounded to metres. No grades per pitch stated. The original report admits uncertain belays and lengths (parts were simul-climbed), so confidence medium.
review.other_findings: Stored grade 5.9 and 7 pitches agree; stated lengths sum to about 270 m vs stored 305.

pitch_detail.notes: Move into a dihedral and up to a ledge, then work the crack system to a large ledge at the foot of a tall right-facing corner.
Climb the corner to a squeeze, a ledge, and a broken roof, then continue up the corner to a belay at the foot of the next wall on a large grassy ledge.
A winding line to a ledge, past a small roof into a very clean corner. Belay on a ledge from a block.
From the belay ledge, mossy twin finger cracks and the wall above lead to scrambling at the top.

review.changed: Wrote all four pitches described, which is one more than the stored count of 3. No bolts or anchors stated beyond a block belay.
review.other_findings: Stored pitches 3, but 4 are described; the stated 25-50 m pitch lengths total about 130 m against a stated 700 feet of climb.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb the centre of the face, keeping a right-facing corner on your right, to a notch; protection is small gear. The line runs between a right-facing and a left-facing corner. Belay in the notch. About 170 feet.
Follow the chimney above the notch, then easier ground to a small ledge or recess about 20 feet below a large roof. About 140 feet.
Trend left, getting over a bulge beside the roof's left end. About 100 feet.

review.changed: Wrote all three pitches. No rappel table: the descent is a walk north up the ridge to a cordelette, one rappel west down a gully to a big block, then downclimbing; not a station list.
review.other_findings: Stored grade 5.8 PG13 consistent; only pitch 1 graded.

pitch_detail.notes: A right-leaning crack with lots of face holds starts the pitch. It pushes through a steep overlap with awkward gear, then veers up and left onto the last three bolts of the neighbouring route Marine Layer, ending at a bolted anchor. Standard rack plus a few bolts and small gear at the crux.
Stemming in the narrow dihedral, clip three bolts; next, shift right onto the face and clip more bolts up to the high point of the headlands.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. No grades, lengths or pitch-1 bolt count given (bolt count there is ambiguous), so left out.

pitch_detail.notes: From the base of the buttress, follow a left-angling crack to a ledge, then traverse left to the foot of a finger crack and build an anchor. Likely goes free at 5.10/10+. Hand-sized gear.

Go about 15 feet up a left-leaning finger crack to place gear, then move 15 feet leftward across the face on good holds. Go up good holds and trend right toward the main crack. Reach the top of the crack through a thin finger pocket: the crux, with little or no protection, around a 5.9 R/X move. Then top out and continue on the regular route. Loose, dirty rock and finger-sized gear only; a bolt or two is wanted here.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. No lengths stated. This is a variation to the start of pitch 3 of Southeast Buttress.
review.other_findings: Stored grade includes A0; description never mentions aid.

pitch_detail.notes: After climbing the vertical cornice to reach the base of the ice, lead the water-ice about 110 feet and belay in the cave.
Squeeze through the cave and climb rock and tuff about 110 feet to a ledge with a bush and a fixed anchor. Descend by rappelling the route.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. Rappel is just 'rap the route', so no table.
review.other_findings: None; stored WI4 M3 Steep Snow agrees.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb over the cauliflower cone, then steep, varied ice to the top. Belay options: a creek boulder set well back from the lip (about 30 feet), or the very large chockstone beyond it. Continue up the winding canyon, right then left, over some easy ice or snow above running water, to the second pitch in a cave.
Climb the tube, then a brief curtain, to the top. For a belay, build one with screws in the gentler ice above, or reach a small tree 30 feet up and to the right.

rappel_detail.anchor: rock pinch under the huge chockstone
rappel_detail.notes: Hike back down to the base of pitch 1 for this rappel.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches and the two-rappel descent. Walking off north above P2 is also possible.

pitch_detail.notes: Steep, well-protected mixed terrain, then the crux transition onto the ice curtain, finishing on lower-angle ice deep in the chimney. Reach the base from Broadway, about halfway between the Notch Couloir and The Window.

Continue up ice at the back of the chimney, then make hard moves out and around a large chockstone. The difficulty eases above but stays real. Finish by traversing right to the base of the second chimney system (Eubank's Chimney).
Straight up Eubank's Chimney; after about 100 feet it meets Upper Kiener's.

review.changed: Wrote all three pitches. Gaining Broadway first is a major undertaking (Lamb's Slide, Alexander's Chimney or Field's Chimney). Gear: stubbies, medium screws, nuts, cams to 3 inches.
review.other_findings: Stored 3 pitches and WI5 M6 agree.

pitch_detail.notes: Several gentler ramps linked by mixed climbing, all on rock gear. It ends at a thin ice spot and a bolted anchor.

Traverse right along the flake, then move onto steep, thin ice for 50 m. The ice thickens near the top but the angle stays vertical or slightly overhanging, so the pitch stays sustained. Use many screws, including stubbies. Early ascents found the first 60 feet of ice protected only by girth-hitched stubbies; it later formed thicker and took 13 cm screws.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. No table for the descent: two double-rope rappels, with two 70 m ropes falling just short of the ground.
review.other_findings: The page repeats its description in slang; ignored the duplicate. Stored 2 pitches agree.

pitch_detail.notes: The start may involve AI2 to 2+ ice or steep snow, leading to a chimney that is hidden from below. The chimney, mostly stemming, is around M1 or easy fifth class; the hard part is about 30 feet, with much easier terrain beyond.

The main gully bends right. Take steep snow or AI2 up to the rock's left side, then find a left-to-right ramp, mostly 3rd and 4th class, to a slabby top-out. The slab is two moves at roughly M2 or 5.5. Belay above in blocky terrain.

Several options at about M1 or easy fifth class: shallow low-angle slab and dihedral straight up, or a ledge to the right first. The slabs are runout with good rests. Join the Keyhole Ridge just below its final 4th class step.

review.changed: Wrote all three pitches. No lengths given. Descent options (walk off Keyhole or Loft, or the Cables with 1 double-rope or 2 single-rope rappels off eyebolts) are not a station list, so no table.

pitch_detail.notes: Choose the most fun rock climbing up to the terrace below the iced chimney. There may be patches of ice.
A short shift of the belay to the base of the icy chimney.
The icy chimney. Gear sits in a chockstone-like feature, with very good placements in the left wall roughly 8 feet higher. The belay is beneath some steps of thin, rolling ice.
Pick the most enjoyable line up the ice.

review.changed: Wrote all four pitches as stated. Protection: regular rock rack, a screw or two, some pins.

pitch_detail.notes: From the top of the boulders, scramble about 15 feet to the base of the corner and build a gear anchor. The pitch ascends a small mossy chimney of loose rock and, in some years, very thin ice, about 50 m. A fixed piton is on your left as you leave the belay. Place nuts and TCUs; screws may go in a thick ice year. Belay below a wide offwidth chimney, after passing a second piton.

Squeeze up the chimney to reach the ice; depending on the year there are about 20 feet of rock first, hard to protect and loose, though large gear is possible. Once on the ice it gets nicer but protection stays hard to find and the climbing feels scary. Gear anchor at the top.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. The report comes from one sighting of the route in lean conditions, hence medium confidence.

pitch_detail.notes: Start at the face's far right end: a slab leads to an ice column set in a corner. Full single rock rack.

The meat starts here: a freestanding ice post roughly 2 by 2 feet and 60 feet tall, then short verglas sections into a moderate chimney with only a few consecutive thin moves before good screw placements. Stubbies went all the way in. Ice is brittle with softer spots at the top of the hard sections. A two-nut anchor was left above and 20 feet right of the top pitch; a 60 m rappel returns to the start.

review.changed: Wrote two pitches; the source is a single trip report, so the split of grades between the two pitches is loose (reported together as M5 and WI4-5). Lengths not stated. No rappel table (only one 60 m rappel).

pitch_detail.notes: Straight up from Alexander's Chimney, passing the wall that guards the gully on the left.
Trend up and slightly right into the main gully. Ice may be good; it was thin with lots of turf, which protects well but offers little other gear. Some simul-climbing was used. About 300 feet.
Follow the gully until it ends under two chimneys, over snow-covered rock steps. The M2+ grade is tentative.
Traverse right up a thin slab (the crux) and stretch the rope to an exposed stance overlooking the huge wall on the left of the Notch Couloir.
A single M3+ move gets you around a block, with a huge drop beneath. Then rap into the Notch if the station can be found, or walk off the back to descend the Loft or Lamb's Slide.

review.changed: Wrote the pitches as labelled: 1, 2, 3-4 combined, 5, 6 (five entries; stored count is 5). Based on a lean-conditions report.
review.other_findings: Good conditions could mean 500 feet of 60-degree ice below and a WI4 chimney at the top, which the stored grade WI3- does not reflect.

pitch_detail.notes: Gain a few metres of broken ground under the Window route's big right-facing corner, then angle rightward across scrappy terrain to a big ledge. Belay anywhere along it, after about 25 m.

Shared with the Wobblisk start to the Obelisk. Shuffle to the ledge's right end and make an awkward move around the corner, aided by two diagonal splitters, to a prominent crack system. Pass a wobbly pillar wedged in a chimney with care. The crux is a delicate switch of cracks leftward; vegetated cracks follow. Past a small chockstone, a brief steep crumbling band reaches a ramp tilting right; belay at the upper right end of the ramp, below the ice.

After a few metres of easy ice, climb the ice fin in the slightly overhanging left-facing corner above the belay (an easier variation lies a few metres left), protected by strenuous but good beaks. Gear above the ice protects moves out of the corner into a deep narrow chimney. Follow the thinly iced chimney with short screws and rock gear, exit left under a roof past a dagger, then zig-zag up narrow ice runnels to the thick ice ledge below the cracks of the headwall. Belay at the top right; pins help.

Go directly up the rightmost crack of the web, a shallow mossy left-facing corner next to the big Obelisk offwidth, with solid hooks, excellent gear and a building pump. Above the small roof, easier ground trends up and a bit left to a wide crack inside a left-facing corner; gear is in the grooves on the right wall. Belay on an excellent ledge under Table Ledge. A harder variation, Baknnator, branches left.

Move right along the ledge to a wide crack at the back of a flake and get on top of it, then easy ground and turf to Table Ledge, which is also the top of the Casual Route. Choices for topping out and descending are many (Kiener's Route, the Loft, rappelling D7 or the Crack of Delight, or the Cables). Nothing is fixed on the route.

review.changed: Wrote all five pitches. No rappel table (descent options only). A 70 m rope is useful for pitch 3, and a tag line for hauling.

skip_reasons.co_ironsides_slab_excitable_boy: No per-pitch text beyond a crux comment on pitch 2 and bolt anchors; not a one-by-one description.
